response.sql: WITH order_avgs AS (SELECT ordersmark, AVG(remaincount) AS avg_remain FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ordersmark), bench1 AS (SELECT AVG(remaincount) AS b1 FROM orderexecutions WHERE remaincount IS NOT NULL), stage1 AS (SELECT o.ordersmark, o.avg_remain FROM order_avgs o CROSS JOIN bench1 WHERE o.avg_remain > bench1.b1), bench2 AS (SELECT AVG(avg_remain) AS b2 FROM stage1), stage2 AS (SELECT s.avg_remain FROM stage1 s CROSS JOIN bench2 WHERE s.avg_remain > bench2.b2) SELECT AVG(s.avg_remain) AS mean_of_remaining_avgs, AVG(s.avg_remain - bench1.b1) AS avg_excess_over_first, AVG(s.avg_remain - bench2.b2) AS avg_excess_over_second FROM stage2 s CROSS JOIN bench1 CROSS JOIN bench2

assumptions.assumption: The first benchmark is the mean of remaincount over all individual non-NULL execution rows (execution-weighted), not the mean of the per-order averages, as the request states.
Executions with a NULL ordersmark are grouped together by GROUP BY as one order; an order whose remaincount values are all NULL is excluded because it has no average.
Comparisons are strict (above means greater than), and no rounding is applied, so the REAL values are returned at full precision.
